extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, communications and measurement teams, and communications managers tracking PR performance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for selecting, tracking, and reporting the most important PR KPIs (earned media, share of voice, sentiment, LLM visibility, etc.) and how to connect them to business outcomes. Includes advertising KPIs, reporting types, and tooling recommendations for PR measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: KPI selection and alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: KPIs must be tied to business impact and organizational goals; an effective KPI is an actionable metric that keeps your strategy on track.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations don’t need too many PR KPIs; determine which metrics are most important to the organization, ensure they are dynamic and measurable, and measure performance against competitors and industry benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage secured by the PR team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track the number of media placements you have at any given time; consider a subset focused on top-tier publications for your industry and audience. Volume of placements is tied with Reach and Impressions as a key metric of PR success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Sum of viewership for publications and websites in which your coverage is featured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reach to understand possible audience size for coverage; combine with other metrics to judge visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share of voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of coverage—for your brand, products, or high-profile executive(s)—compared to competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include several competitors to gauge your place within the industry or benchmark one at a time and drill into coverage to uncover differentiators. Share of voice can be tracked by volume or reach (a competitor may have higher mention volume while you appear in higher-reach publications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Social engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: How many shares and social comments the coverage you generate receives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure engagement to understand how coverage resonates and is distributed socially; include shares, comments, and other interaction metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Tone of the articles mentioning your brand or competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sentiment analysis to see whether your brand is creating positive or negative associations. Tip: Learn how to perform sentiment analysis to improve accuracy and interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of press releases and pitches you are sending out and how they are performing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track outreach volume along with coverage generated and relationship-building progress with journalists. Use distribution tools to measure open rates and internal links clicked. Tip: Use press release templates and pitching best practices to improve performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The placement of your brand mention (headline, body) and its prominence in the article’s content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess prominence (headline vs body), depth of coverage, and whether key messages are included. Tip: Learn how to measure and analyze media coverage to evaluate quality beyond volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Volume of coverage based on location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess success at targeting key geographical demographics and markets by measuring coverage distribution across regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key message penetration
rubrics_metrics.description: Break your coverage down by key themes and measure how strongly you are associated with each one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure which themes your competitors are associated with and compare results to understand message dominance and gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall media presence
rubrics_metrics.description: A snapshot of your competitive landscape by combining share of voice and sentiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use combined metrics to get a holistic view of presence and perception versus competitors. Tip: Conduct a media impact analysis for deeper insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earned traffic
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of visitors that were driven to your website as a result of your earned coverage and link placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute website visits to earned media and links to demonstrate direct behavioral impact and downstream conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain authority
rubrics_metrics.description: A metric that predicts how well a website will rank on search engines (measured on a logarithmic scale from 1 to 100).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Securing link placement on third-party sites with high domain authority can improve your site's SEO. Use domain authority checkers to track changes over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: PR’s success in driving event attendance, garnering media coverage of events, and building relationships with speakers and attendees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track attendance lift, media mentions tied to events, and relationship-building outcomes as KPIs for event-focused PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure how quickly PR gets things back to normal during a crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmark volume and sentiment to baseline levels from before the crisis started; track speed of reputation recovery and message correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM Visibility (KPI)
rubrics_metrics.description: How often and how accurately your brand appears in AI-generated responses (such as ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, and other generative search experiences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LLM visibility indicates whether earned media, brand mentions, and authoritative content are being picked up and cited by AI systems. Strong visibility signals trusted-source recognition; weak visibility may signal gaps in coverage, authority, or content structure. Tip: Learn PR GEO strategies and press release optimization for LLMs.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC (cost-per-click)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost-per-click — measures campaign-level performance (which creative or message drives clicks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPC helps understand click-driving performance but doesn't reveal post-click behavior (conversions). Optimizing only for low CPC may emphasize quantity over quality; analyze down-funnel performance to assess true value.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA (cost per acquisition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost-per-acquisition — determines the cost of the action a user takes to convert (e.g., sign-up, form fill, purchase).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPA gives a more comprehensive view of acquisition success and helps evaluate whether paid media delivers a return. Use CPA to compare acquisition efficiency across channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTR (click-through-rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ratio of users who click on a specific link to the number of total users who view a page, email, or advertisement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CTR measures immediate engagement with creative or messaging; use it to compare variants and optimize creatives, but combine with downstream metrics to assess business impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROAS (return on advertising spend)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures whether the costs of acquisition efforts are worth their expenditure by dividing the revenue generated by those costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ROAS indicates overall return (expressed as a multiple or percentage). Focusing on ROAS can justify higher CPA if overall return is strong; balance ROAS with CPA to make informed optimization decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective-specific reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports that show the impact of your brand, campaign or product based on the KPIs you set out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these reports to answer whether you increased sales, brand awareness, or engagement. Benchmark against previous campaigns, brand awareness efforts, or influencer performance. Media monitoring tools help gather the necessary data; follow-up analysis post-campaign is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-specific reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports that focus on how successful your objectives were over a specified period of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use time windows to spot trends (e.g., spikes on particular days, evening/weekend patterns) and to measure campaign momentum and timing effects. Helpful for detecting lagged traction or campaign-specific timing nuances.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM visibility PR reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports that surface how often a brand appears in AI answers, which sources influence those outputs, and whether key messaging is accurately reflected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reports help PR teams understand which earned placements shape AI narratives, identify gaps or mischaracterizations, benchmark against competitors, and prioritize earned media likely to influence generative responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Right Tools to Measure PR ROI
rubrics_metrics.description: Use media monitoring platforms, analytics dashboards, and reporting tools that unify earned, owned, and paid metrics to quantify campaign impact and prove ROI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize yourself with tools other departments use and overlapping goals. Comprehensive platforms (e.g., Meltwater) provide automated reporting and deeper analysis; advanced capabilities (GenAI Lens) allow analysis of brand appearance in generative AI. Only some PR teams have all needed tools—measure tool gaps and integrate cross-departmental analytics.

rubrics_metrics.name: PR ROI measurement (connecting to business outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate PR ROI by connecting earned media to website traffic, lead generation, conversions, and brand awareness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine media monitoring, analytics tools, and attribution models to link PR activities to downstream business metrics. Use objective-specific and time-specific reports to make the connection concrete for stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: PR report components
rubrics_metrics.description: Essential elements a PR report should include to prove performance and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong PR report typically includes: media coverage and reach; share of voice; sentiment analysis; website traffic and conversions; key campaign highlights; and LLM visibility insights. Use real-time dashboards for fast-moving situations and monthly/quarterly reports for regular cadence.
